title: Science and Technology
description: The only theme of the book with no Arts lesson, so its two lessons run straight on: four readers of a website disagreeing about how much time online is too much, with the words of a life online (online addiction, to surf the net, cyberspace, to chat in its newer sense of typing in real time, a chat room, the escape key, to survive, depression, irrational, to break up, to conceal, to acknowledge) and one reader whose message tells a harm and defends a need at the same time, so that no column will hold her; reported speech and its three shifts - the person, the tense stepping back one notch when the reporting verb is past, and the words of time and place - together with the two tenses that never move because there is nowhere further back to go, the difference between say and tell, the cases where the backshift does not happen because what was said is still true, and a warning about the model sentence the book itself prints; a recording in which a specialist in futuristic studies describes the human being of fifty thousand years from now - taller, with a larger forehead and stronger eyes, with weaker limbs, more sensitive fingers and no hair at all - and the exception that closes it, since he will still have thoughts and emotions like ours; the vocabulary of that future (futuristic, obvious, to assume, substantial, bald, emotions, capacity); gradual change with more and more, less and less and the short cousin -er and -er whose meaning the printed grammar box leaves blank, and the distinction that decides half the marks, between one thing changing steadily and two changes tied to each other; and word stress, with the endings that fix it and the suffix that moves it
